destinations.name: Boracay
destinations.summary: A four-kilometre beach that was closed for six months and rebuilt, now capped at 19,215 people at a time and routinely blowing straight through it.
destinations.headline: Boracay in 2026: the rehabilitation worked, the carrying capacity does not, and the fees keep going up
destinations.body: Boracay is a 10.32 square kilometre island off the northwest coast of Panay, home to 37,802 people at the 2020 census, and famous almost entirely for one four-kilometre stretch of sand called White Beach, split by convention into Stations 1, 2 and 3. Its reputation is genuine: Conde Nast Traveler ranked it the number one island in the world in 2014, and it was named the world's second-best beach in 2012. Its problems are equally documented. Coral cover around the island fell 70.5 percent between 1988 and 2011, a coliform bacteria spike drove a 60 percent drop in tourists as far back as 1997, and in 2018 President Duterte called the island a cesspool and shut it to tourists entirely from April 26 to October 26, 2018. That six-month closure was not cosmetic. The sewage system was overhauled, illegal structures were demolished, a 30-metre buffer zone was established from the waterline, and the beach was cleared of masseuses, vendors and bonfires. It largely worked, and arrivals recovered to 2,077,977 in 2024 and 2,155,217 in 2025. The unresolved part is the cap. During the closure the Department of Environment and Natural Resources set the island's ecological carrying capacity at 19,215 people present at any given time. That number has been breached every Holy Week since 2022, and 2026 was no exception: even with a four percent dip in Semana Santa visitors, arrivals hit 21,252 on April 14 and 22,519 on April 15, 2026, both well past the limit. In other words the island is managed on paper and oversubscribed in practice, at precisely the weeks most people want to go. The other running story is money. Entry now involves a stack of local fees rather than one: the Malay local government charges a terminal fee of P300, an environmental fee of P150 for domestic and P300 for foreign visitors, boat transfer of P50 to P100, land transport from P150 to P700, and assorted activity fees, and on March 1, 2026 it raised the digital-payment convenience fee on the Boracay i-Pass cashless system from P35 to P85, projected to bring in at least P85 million a year from a million tourists. Interior Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla ordered the LGU in February 2025 to cut fees or impose a collection moratorium; as of March 2026 the LGU had publicly refused to budge. Practical arrival is still simple: fly into Caticlan (MPH), take a five to ten minute tricycle or van to the Caticlan Jetty Port for around P75, pay the fees at the terminal windows, and cross by pump boat in five to fifteen minutes for about P50. Environmental management continues, with bans on single-use plastics, restrictions on smoking and drinking on the beach, promotion of reef-safe sunscreen and regulated boat access, and electric tricycles replacing the old two-stroke fleet behind the beach. A proposed bridge to the mainland has drawn public warnings from experts and a counter-request from the local community for a hospital instead.
destinations.what_great:
White Beach deserves its reputation. Four kilometres of fine white sand with genuinely calm, swimmable water is a rare combination, and the 2018 rehabilitation removed the things that were ruining it, the beachfront structures, the vendors, the masseuses and the bonfires, and imposed a 30-metre buffer from the waterline that has kept the sand itself open. The sewage overhaul addressed the actual cause of the closure rather than the optics of it.

The island is also easy and cheap to reach once you know the drill: Caticlan airport to the jetty port runs about P75, and the crossing is a five to fifteen minute pump-boat ride for roughly P50. Stations 1, 2 and 3 give you meaningfully different price and noise levels on the same beach, Bulabog on the other side is a serious kiteboarding and windsurfing spot, and the electric tricycles have taken a real bite out of the noise and fumes behind the beach.
destinations.what_ruined:
The cap is the story. The DENR set the island's carrying capacity at 19,215 people at any given time during the 2018 closure, and it has been breached every Holy Week since 2022, including in 2026 when arrivals hit 21,252 on April 14 and 22,519 on April 15 despite a four percent dip in Semana Santa visitors. A limit that is exceeded every year at the same predictable moment is a limit in name only, and with arrivals at 2,155,217 in 2025 the pressure is not easing.

The fee stack is the other complaint, and it is getting worse rather than better. Between a P300 terminal fee, an environmental fee of P150 domestic or P300 foreign, boat transfer, land transport from P150 to P700, activity fees and the digital convenience fee that jumped from P35 to P85 on March 1, 2026, the cost of simply arriving adds up before you have bought anything. The national Interior Secretary ordered the Malay LGU in February 2025 to cut fees or pause collection and the LGU publicly refused, so this is unlikely to resolve soon. On top of that, seasonal green algae blooms hit the beach from February through May, coral cover fell 70.5 percent between 1988 and 2011 and has not been restored, and a proposed bridge to the mainland has drawn expert warnings, with the local community asking for a hospital instead.
tips: Do not go during Holy Week. The island's 19,215-person carrying capacity has been breached every Holy Week since 2022, and in 2026 arrivals hit 21,252 on April 14 and 22,519 on April 15.

Budget for the fee stack at the jetty port, not just the airfare: a P300 terminal fee, an environmental fee of P150 for domestic and P300 for foreign visitors, and a P50 to P100 boat transfer, paid at separate windows in Caticlan.
Expect the cashless system. Malay's Executive Order No. 45 of December 3, 2025 mandates cashless payment through Boracay i-Pass, and the convenience fee rose from P35 to P85 on March 1, 2026.
Avoid February through May if algae bothers you. Seasonal green algae blooms wash up on White Beach during those months; they are natural and harmless but they are not the postcard.
Pick your Station deliberately. Station 1 is the widest sand and the priciest, Station 2 is the busy commercial middle, and Station 3 is the quieter budget end of the same four-kilometre beach.
Bring reef-safe sunscreen and skip single-use plastics. Both are part of the post-2018 rules, alongside restrictions on smoking and drinking on the beach and regulated boat access.

guide.title: Boracay Travel Guide: Fees, Ferries and When Not to Go in 2026
guide.summary: How to get to Boracay, what the layered local fees actually cost in 2026, and how to time a trip around the carrying-capacity breaches and algae season.
guide.body:
Getting to Boracay is a short, well-worn chain with a toll booth in the middle. Fly into Caticlan (MPH), take a five to ten minute tricycle or van to the Caticlan Jetty Port for around P75, clear the fee windows, then cross to the island by pump boat in roughly five to fifteen minutes for about P50. Ferry service runs around the clock, with scheduled departures every 30 to 60 minutes between about 5:00 AM and 8:00 PM and boats outside those hours waiting to fill.

The fees are where people get caught out, because there is no single ticket. The Malay local government's schedule includes a terminal fee of P300, an environmental fee of P150 for domestic visitors and P300 for foreign visitors, boat transfer of P50 to P100, land transport from P150 to P700, and separate charges for activities such as snorkeling. Payment is cashless: Mayor Frolibar Bautista signed Executive Order No. 45 on December 3, 2025 mandating the Boracay i-Pass system, and on March 1, 2026 the digital payment convenience fee rose from P35 to P85, a change projected to collect at least P85 million a year from roughly a million tourists. This is contested rather than settled. Interior Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla ordered the LGU in February 2025 to reduce fees or impose a collection moratorium; as of March 2026 the Department of Tourism's regional director confirmed the LGU would not budge, so plan on paying the current schedule.

Timing matters more than anything else here. The DENR set the island's ecological carrying capacity at 19,215 people present at any time during the 2018 rehabilitation, and it has been exceeded every Holy Week since 2022, most recently on April 14 and 15, 2026 at 21,252 and 22,519 arrivals despite Semana Santa visitor numbers dipping four percent year on year. The peak season, Amihan, runs roughly Christmas through February and brings the calmest water on the White Beach side. February through May brings seasonal green algae blooms onto the sand, harmless but unattractive. That leaves the shoulder weeks of late November and early December, or the quieter stretches outside Philippine holidays, as the sensible windows. On the island itself, the post-2018 rules still apply: a 30-metre buffer from the waterline keeps the beach clear of structures, single-use plastics are banned, smoking and drinking on the beach are restricted, reef-safe sunscreen is promoted and boat access is regulated, and electric tricycles have replaced much of the old fleet on the back road.

rating_rationale.overall: A genuinely world-class beach that was properly rehabilitated in 2018, marked down because the carrying capacity meant to protect it is breached every peak season and the algae months cover a third of the year.
rating_rationale.safety: Boracay is a heavily policed tourism zone with no particular violent-crime issue for visitors; the realistic risks are sea and boat conditions during the habagat months, crowd crush at peak periods when the island exceeds its 19,215-person capacity, and ordinary petty theft.
rating_rationale.value: Accommodation and food span every budget, but arrival costs stack up fast, a P300 terminal fee, P150 domestic or P300 foreign environmental fee, P50 to P100 boat transfer, P150 to P700 land transport, plus a convenience fee raised from P35 to P85 on March 1, 2026.

destinations.name: Budapest
destinations.summary: Budapest's baths and ruin bars are the real deal, but a well documented taxi and bar overcharging scam targets tourists in the same nightlife district after dark.
destinations.headline: Budapest's Thermal Baths and Ruin Bars Are Worth It, But Watch for the Well Documented Tourist Bar Scam
destinations.body:
Budapest's thermal baths are not a tourist gimmick, they are a genuinely old civic institution built on more than 100 medicinal geothermal springs beneath the city, and Szechenyi Thermal Bath in City Park is the flagship. It opened on June 16, 1913, was designed by architect Gyozo Czigler in Neo-Baroque style, and draws water from two springs at 74C and 77C. The complex has 3 outdoor and 15 indoor pools ranging across roughly 18C to 38C, underwent a full renovation between 1999 and 2009, and is regularly described as the largest medicinal bath complex in Europe. Gellert Baths, across the river inside a historic Art Nouveau hotel, is the other major draw. Neither bath's official ticket office publishes an easy English price list online, both of their pricing pages returned access errors during this research, and the walk up ticket at the gate is reliably cheaper than what third party booking platforms charge, where a full day Szechenyi entry was listed starting around US$52.98. Buy directly at the bath if you can.

The ruin bar scene has real history behind it, it is not just marketing. Szimpla Kert, the movement's most famous survivor, is widely credited as the pioneer of the concept, with the first documented ruin bar opening on Kertesz utca in 2002. The idea exploded in 2004 when Abel Zsendovits converted a condemned building on Kazinczy Street into what became the template: abandoned buildings, mismatched furniture, exposed decay, and cheap drinks, clustered mostly in District VII, the old Jewish Quarter also known as Erzsebetvaros. Two decades later that neighborhood is the center of Budapest's nightlife, and it is also where the well documented tourist scam below concentrates.

Getting around is cheap by Western European standards. A single BKK ticket for one metro, bus, tram, or cogwheel railway ride costs 500 forints, and the M1 Millennium Underground, opened in 1896, was continental Europe's first metro line; the whole metro and tram network now moves about 2.2 million riders a day. The Airport Express bus, line 100E, costs 2,200 forints one way as of mid 2025. For visitors stacking multiple museums and rides, the Budapest Card bundles unlimited public transport (the 100E airport bus excluded), free one time admission to more than 30 attractions including the Hungarian National Museum and the Palvolgyi Cave, one entry to Lukacs Spa, a Danube boat trip, two English language guided walking tours, and discounts at more than 100 other venues, sold in 24, 48, 72, and 96 hour versions and activated on first use. Booked through a resale travel platform the shortest version started around US$60.72, so compare that against buying transit tickets and museum entries separately before assuming the card saves money.

The city's most persistent tourist trap is not a myth, and it is documented by both the UK Foreign Office and the US State Department: certain taxi drivers earn a commission for steering visitors, especially at night, toward specific bars, clubs, and restaurants that then present wildly inflated bills for food and drink, sometimes escorting people who cannot pay to the nearest cash machine. Official guidance is blunt, ask to see a priced menu before you order anything, walk away from venues that will not show one, and treat any unsolicited bar recommendation from a taxi driver or a stranger on the street as a red flag rather than a friendly tip. Licensed Fotaxi cabs run on a regulated meter, base fare 1,300 forints plus 521 forints per kilometer and 130 forints per minute waiting, with an 800 forint surcharge from the airport as of August 2026, numbers worth knowing before you get in any car.

None of this has slowed Budapest down. The city logged about 7 million international overnight visitors in 2025, and it is set to host the 2026 UEFA Champions League final, both of which mean higher prices and thicker crowds at the baths and in the Jewish Quarter than a shoulder season visit would bring. Wikivoyage flags mid September through late October as the better window, less rain, long sunny days, and more moderate temperatures than the sticky summer months when every pool and ruin bar courtyard is packed.
destinations.what_great:
The baths are the real deal, not a spa marketing exercise. Szechenyi's Neo-Baroque courtyards, opened in 1913 and drawing on natural springs as hot as 77C, plus 3 outdoor and 15 indoor pools, are historic architecture doubling as a functioning public bath, not a theme park built to look old. The ruin bar scene has equally real roots, Szimpla Kert and its neighbors trace back to a documented 2002 to 2004 origin of converting condemned buildings in the Jewish Quarter, rather than being a manufactured tourist product.

Transit is cheap and historically significant at the same time, a single ride is 500 forints and the M1 line that runs toward City Park is continental Europe's oldest metro, opened in 1896. The Budapest Card, bought carefully, genuinely bundles a lot of value, unlimited transit, 30 plus attractions, a Danube boat trip, and two guided walks into one pass for travelers who plan to move fast.
destinations.what_ruined:
The scam that keeps showing up in official government travel advisories is real and specifically targets tourists at night: taxi drivers paid on commission steer visitors toward bars and clubs that hand over inflated bills and, per the UK and US advisories, have escorted non paying customers to an ATM. That risk sits in the same Jewish Quarter blocks where the authentic ruin bars are, so it is easy to wander from Szimpla Kert into a lookalike trap without knowing the difference.

Pricing transparency is also weaker than it should be, the official bath websites for both Szechenyi and Gellert were not accessible during this research, and third party platforms sell Szechenyi's full day entry from roughly US$52.98 and the Budapest Card from about US$60.72, both almost certainly marked up over a walk up ticket. Add in a 2026 Champions League final and a 2025 visitor count near 7 million, and popular spots will run more crowded and pricier than an off season search suggests.
tips: Only get into licensed Fotaxi cabs, the regulated meter runs 1,300 forints base fare plus 521 forints per kilometer and 130 forints per minute waiting, with an 800 forint airport surcharge as of August 2026.

Treat any bar or club recommendation from a taxi driver or a stranger on the street as a red flag, both the UK Foreign Office and US State Department document a commission based scam that funnels tourists into venues with inflated bills.
Ask to see a priced menu before ordering anything at a bar in the Jewish Quarter, and leave if the venue won't show one, per official government travel guidance.
A single BKK metro, bus, or tram ticket is 500 forints, cheaper than assuming you need the 2,200 forint Airport Express (line 100E) for every trip.

Compare the Budapest Card against buying separately, resale platforms list it starting around US$60.72 for the shortest duration, and it excludes the 100E airport bus even though it covers the rest of transit plus 30 plus attractions.

Visit Szimpla Kert or the Kazinczy utca ruin bar cluster in District VII (Erzsebetvaros) for the genuine version of the scene, which traces back to a documented 2002 to 2004 origin, rather than an imitation set up to look old.

Go in the shoulder season, mid September through late October, Wikivoyage notes less rain and long sunny days, and it will beat the crowds tied to 2025's roughly 7 million international overnight visitors and the 2026 Champions League final.

guide.title: Budapest Practical Guide: Baths, Transit, and Staying Out of Tourist Traps
guide.summary: How to get around Budapest, when to go, which neighborhoods matter, and how to avoid paying tourist markup on baths, cards, and bar tabs.
guide.body:
Public transport is the easiest way to move through Budapest and one of its genuine bargains, a single BKK ticket covers one ride on the metro, bus, tram, or cogwheel railway for 500 forints, and the M1 Millennium Underground that runs toward City Park and the baths is continental Europe's oldest metro line, opened in 1896. The metro and tram network together move roughly 2.2 million passengers a day, so it is built for exactly the kind of point to point movement visitors need. The Airport Express, line 100E, runs 2,200 forints one way, worth knowing so you are not surprised at the airport.

City Park in Pest holds Szechenyi Thermal Bath, and the Buda side across the Danube holds Gellert Baths, so a bath day usually anchors whichever half of the city you are already exploring. The Jewish Quarter, District VII or Erzsebetvaros, is the ruin bar center and the origin point of the entire genre, dating to a documented 2002 to 2004 stretch when condemned buildings on and around Kazinczy Street were converted into bars. It is also, not coincidentally, where the taxi and bar overcharging scam documented by UK and US travel advisories concentrates, so treat unsolicited venue recommendations there with suspicion.

On money, buy transit tickets and bath entry directly where you can rather than through resale platforms, which listed a Szechenyi full day ticket from about US$52.98 and the shortest Budapest Card from about US$60.72, both likely above the walk up price. Time the trip for mid September through late October if you can, Wikivoyage flags that window for less rain and long sunny days, ahead of the crowd spike expected for the 2026 UEFA Champions League final and building on 2025's roughly 7 million international overnight visitors.

rating_rationale.overall: Genuinely historic baths and an authentic ruin bar origin story earn a strong score, docked one point for opaque bath pricing and scam risk.
rating_rationale.safety: Violent crime is not the concern, but a well documented commission based bar and taxi overcharging scam targeting tourists at night is real enough to cost a point.
rating_rationale.value: Public transit and the Budapest Card can be a genuine deal, but resale ticket markups and scam bars in the same nightlife district drag the score down.

destinations.name: Buenos Aires
destinations.summary: Buenos Aires is a genuine bargain for anyone spending dollars or euros right now, but counterfeit-bill street scams and creeping inflation friction take a bite out of the fun.
destinations.headline: Buenos Aires 2026: World-Class Steak and Tango on a Weak Peso, But Watch for the Fake-Cop Currency Scam
destinations.body: Argentina's currency situation has actually stabilized compared to the chaos of a few years ago, and that matters for anyone planning a trip. In April 2025 the Milei government lifted most of the long-standing 'cepo' currency controls, backed by a $20 billion IMF deal, and for the first time in six years Argentines could buy dollars freely at the official rate. The result is that the official rate, the parallel 'blue dollar' rate, and the MEP rate, once wildly different, have converged. By July 2026 all three sit in a tight band of roughly 1,460 to 1,530 pesos per dollar, with the gap between official and blue under 15 percent, a huge change from the 100-plus percent spreads tourists used to arbitrage in cash exchange houses. A new monetary regime that started January 2, 2026 adjusts the exchange rate bands monthly in line with inflation data, so the rate keeps drifting even if it is no longer a two-tier mess. Inflation itself is still real: annual CPI ran about 33.5 percent in June 2026, down dramatically from 211 percent at the end of 2023, but monthly inflation has been stuck near 1.9 to 2.9 percent, and the central bank's own survey put the year-end 2026 forecast at roughly 30 percent. Milei's campaign promise to fully dollarize the economy has quietly been shelved, he has said outright that Argentines don't want it, so the peso remains the day-to-day currency with dollars used alongside it under a 'currency competition' framework. For visitors, all this converts into real value. A tango dinner show runs roughly 70 to 150 dollars per person at venues like El Querandi, El Viejo Almacen, or Cafe de los Angelitos, while a show-only ticket without dinner averages closer to 40 dollars since the performance itself is identical either way. A 500-gram steak at a neighborhood parrilla can run about 10 dollars, with upscale cuts at nicer steakhouses landing between 35 and 70 dollars. Getting around is cheap too: a Subte ride costs roughly 30 to 60 cents with a SUBE card versus about a dollar tapping a foreign credit card directly, and taxi meters start around 300 pesos plus about 60 pesos per kilometer. The friction is on the safety and hassle side. Argentina sits at a Level 1 to 2 travel advisory, but petty theft, phone snatching, bag grabs, and pickpocket teams working Subte lines A and B during rush hour, is genuinely common in San Telmo, La Boca, Palermo, and around the Obelisco and Plaza de Mayo. The bigger trap for tourists is the counterfeit-bill con: people posing as plainclothes police stop travelers on Florida Street, Lavalle, or near Plaza de Mayo, claim they need to inspect cash for fakes, and swap real notes for counterfeits or simply pocket bills. Real Argentine police do not stop pedestrians to inspect their wallets. As of July 1, 2026, Argentina also started requiring all foreign visitors to carry travel health insurance with at least 20,000 dollars in coverage, including emergency evacuation, which is a new line item to sort out before departure even though the 90-day visa-free entry for US citizens itself remains free.
destinations.what_great:
Buenos Aires is one of the best value cities in the Americas right now if you are earning and spending in dollars or euros. Currency convergence since the April 2025 reforms means you no longer need to hunt for a good blue-dollar exchange rate, the official rate is close enough to fair that ATMs and cards work fine, and that fair rate stretches a long way on parrilla steak, wine, and tango. A neighborhood steakhouse serving a half-kilo cut for around 10 dollars, or a full tango dinner show for well under what a comparable night out costs in New York or London, is a real and repeatable experience, not a one-off deal. The Subte is cheap and functional with a SUBE card, the city is dense and walkable, and the culture, architecture, and food scene hold up on their own merits independent of the exchange rate.

The broader macro story is also genuinely improving rather than static. Inflation has fallen from 211 percent annually in 2023 to roughly 33 percent by mid-2026, and the multi-tier currency system that used to confuse and occasionally trap tourists has largely collapsed into one workable rate. That is a meaningfully calmer environment to visit in than Buenos Aires offered even two years ago.
destinations.what_ruined:
The instability has not disappeared, it has just moved from the exchange rate to the street. The single biggest tourist-targeted scam in Buenos Aires right now is people posing as plainclothes police on Florida Street, Lavalle, and around Plaza de Mayo who claim they need to check your cash for counterfeits, then swap your real pesos for fake ones or simply steal them outright. Ordinary pickpocketing and phone-snatching are also up in San Telmo, La Boca, Palermo, and on crowded Subte cars, especially lines A and B during peak hours, and using a phone near a curb or open train door is a specific, named risk in most current safety writeups.

On the money side, monthly inflation is still running close to 2 to 3 percent, and the exchange rate bands now adjust monthly rather than staying fixed, so the good pricing tourists enjoy is a moving target rather than a locked-in deal, and it is genuinely painful for Argentines living on peso salaries even as it is a gift to foreign visitors. Add a brand-new requirement, as of July 1, 2026, for all foreign visitors to carry travel health insurance with at least 20,000 dollars in coverage, and there is now an extra pre-trip logistics step that did not exist a year earlier.
tips: Load a SUBE card for the Subte, it runs roughly 30 to 60 cents per ride versus about a dollar when tapping a foreign credit card directly at the turnstile.

If budget matters, book a tango show-only ticket (around 40 dollars) instead of the dinner package (70 to 150 dollars) at venues like El Querandi or Cafe de los Angelitos, the performance itself is identical either way.

Never hand your wallet or cash to anyone on Florida Street, Lavalle, or near Plaza de Mayo who claims to be plainclothes police checking for counterfeit bills, genuine Argentine police do not stop pedestrians to inspect currency.
As of July 1, 2026, Argentina requires all foreign visitors to carry travel health insurance with at least 20,000 dollars in coverage, including emergency evacuation, arrange this before you fly.
Keep your phone away from open Subte doors and street curbs, snatch-and-grab theft is a specifically named risk on lines A and B during rush hour and at traffic lights.
The peso still moves, exchange bands now adjust monthly with inflation, so check the current official and blue dollar rate the morning you plan to withdraw or exchange a larger amount.

guide.title: Buenos Aires Travel Guide 2026: Money, Transit, and Neighborhoods
guide.summary: A practical rundown of how to move around Buenos Aires, when to visit, which neighborhoods to base yourself in, and how to avoid the currency traps that snag first-time visitors.
guide.body:
Getting around is straightforward and cheap once you have a SUBE card, which you load with pesos and tap on the Subte, city buses (colectivos), and some suburban trains, it costs roughly 30 to 60 cents a ride versus about a dollar when a foreign card is tapped directly. Taxis and rideshares like Uber and Cabify are widely available and inexpensive by international standards, with meters starting around 300 pesos and adding roughly 60 pesos per kilometer, and airport transfers to or from Ezeiza typically run 40 to 60 dollars. The Subte is efficient for central neighborhoods but lines A and B get crowded at rush hour, which is exactly when pickpocket teams are most active, so keep bags zipped and phones off the curb edge.

Seasonally, Buenos Aires sits in the Southern Hemisphere, so its summer (December to February) is hot and humid while its autumn and spring, March to May and September to November, bring milder, more comfortable weather and are generally considered the best times to visit. Winter (June to August) is cool but rarely harsh, and it is also low season, meaning hotel rates soften.

For neighborhoods, Palermo is the most tourist-friendly base with restaurants, nightlife, and green space, but stay alert there too since it shows up repeatedly in current theft advisories. San Telmo has cobblestone charm, antiques markets, and tango history, and it doubles as one of the more theft-prone areas, especially around its Sunday street fair. Recoleta is quieter, upscale, and close to the famous cemetery. Puerto Madero is the newest, most polished, and safest-feeling district, home to premium tango venues like Rojo Tango, though also the most expensive.

On money, the biggest change in years is that Argentina's official, blue-market, and MEP dollar rates converged after the April 2025 reform that ended the old cepo currency controls, so there is far less reason to hunt for a black-market cash exchange than there used to be, and doing so now mainly adds counterfeit-bill risk rather than meaningfully better pricing. Carry small denomination pesos, verify any large bill you receive, and never let a stranger who claims to be a police officer handle your cash on the street.

rating_rationale.overall: World-class food and culture at a real discount for foreign visitors, docked a point for active tourist-targeted scams that require constant low-grade vigilance.
rating_rationale.safety: Level 1-2 advisory with rare violent crime against tourists, but frequent petty theft and a well-documented fake-police counterfeit-currency scam concentrated in specific tourist zones.
rating_rationale.value: Post-2025 currency convergence plus 33 percent inflation versus a slower-moving exchange rate means dollar and euro spenders get parrilla steak, tango shows, and transit at a steep discount.

facts_checked: April 2025: Milei government lifted most currency controls (the cepo), backed by a $20 billion IMF agreement
By July 2026 official, blue, and MEP peso rates converged to roughly 1,460-1,530 ARS per USD, gap under 15%
Argentina annual inflation was about 33.5% in June 2026, down from 211% in December 2023
New monetary regime started January 2, 2026 with exchange rate bands adjusted monthly in line with inflation
Milei has publicly shelved full dollarization, stating Argentines don't want it
Tango dinner shows run roughly $70-150 per person in 2026; show-only tickets average around $40
Named tango venues: El Querandi, El Viejo Almacen, Cafe de los Angelitos, Tango Porteno, Rojo Tango at Faena
Neighborhood parrilla 500g steak runs about $10 USD; upscale cuts run $35-70
Argentina carries a US State Department Level 1 (with some caution language) travel advisory
Counterfeit-bill and fake-police wallet-inspection scams reported on Florida Street, Lavalle, and near Plaza de Mayo
Pickpocket activity reported concentrated on Subte lines A and B during peak hours
SUBE card Subte fare is roughly $0.30-0.63/ride versus about $1.05 tapping a credit card directly
Taxi meters start around 300 pesos plus about 60 pesos per kilometer; airport transfers run $40-60
US citizens get visa-free entry to Argentina for up to 90 days; the reciprocity fee was eliminated in 2016
As of July 1, 2026, Argentina requires foreign visitors to carry travel health insurance with minimum $20,000 USD coverage

destinations.name: Cairo
destinations.summary: The pyramids and the new Grand Egyptian Museum are worth the trip, but expect relentless touts, thick traffic pollution, and a ticketing system that now wants your card, not your cash.
destinations.headline: Cairo in 2026: The Pyramids Deliver, the New Museum Impresses, and the Hustle Never Stops
destinations.body:
Cairo's headline attraction hasn't changed in 4,500 years, but how you pay to see it has. The Giza Plateau's general admission ticket for foreign adults now runs 700 EGP, with foreign students at 350 EGP and children under six free. That gets you into the open-air complex, the Sphinx enclosure, the Valley Temple of Khafre and the panoramic desert viewpoints, but not inside the pyramids themselves. Climbing into the Great Pyramid of Khufu costs an extra 1,000 EGP for adults on top of the entry fee, while Khafre's interior is 280 EGP and Menkaure's is 200 EGP. Nearly every official ticket window at major sites has also gone card-only, so a fistful of Egyptian pounds will not get you past the gate the way it used to.

The long-awaited Grand Egyptian Museum near the plateau opened to the public on November 4, 2025, and by December it had switched entirely to online, timed-entry booking, meaning walk-up purchases are no longer possible. Foreign adult admission runs about 1,500 EGP, roughly 30 US dollars at 2026 exchange rates, against 200 EGP for Egyptian nationals. It is the first time Tutankhamun's full treasure collection has been displayed together in one place, and it is genuinely the best reason to plan a Cairo trip right now.

Getting to and from the sites is where the honest friction starts. The Giza touts are as persistent as their reputation suggests: the fake 'free photo' handoff followed by a payment demand, the 'this entrance is closed, follow me' redirect, and the classic camel or horse ride that gets quoted low and then repriced tenfold once you're stranded on the animal are all still active scams tourists report running into daily. A firm, immediate no and walking straight to the official ticket kiosk avoids most of it.

Cairo's air is a separate, less avoidable problem. The city has repeatedly ranked among the most polluted major cities in the world through 2025, with annual PM2.5 levels around 39.9 micrograms per cubic meter, nearly eight times the World Health Organization's guideline, driven largely by an aging vehicle fleet stuck in near-permanent traffic congestion. Anyone with respiratory sensitivity should factor that into how many days they spend outdoors in the city center versus at the plateau, which sits on the edge of town with somewhat clearer air.

On safety, the US State Department keeps Egypt at a Level 2, 'Exercise Increased Caution,' rating, with a Do Not Travel warning limited to North and Middle Sinai and parts of the Western Desert, areas nowhere near standard Cairo or Giza itineraries. The embassy has issued periodic security alerts through early 2026 urging visitors to stay alert in public spaces and avoid demonstrations, standard advice for a major capital rather than a reason to cancel a trip. Money-wise, the Egyptian pound has been trading in the low-to-mid 50s against the dollar through 2026 while domestic inflation sits around 14 percent, so prices quoted in pounds can feel like they're moving under your feet even as your dollars or euros still stretch reasonably far.
destinations.what_great:
The Grand Egyptian Museum is the real headline here. Since opening on November 4, 2025, it has finally given Tutankhamun's roughly 5,000-piece collection a single dedicated home, something Cairo never had before, and it sits within sight of the pyramids themselves. The plateau's 700 EGP general admission still buys access to the Sphinx, the Valley Temple and unobstructed views of all three main pyramids, and the desert setting at sunrise or late afternoon, before the midday heat and haze peak, remains one of the most genuinely awe-inducing experiences in travel.

The currency situation, while volatile, currently favors visitors carrying dollars or euros, and museum and monument admission prices, even after 2026 increases, are still inexpensive by major-capital standards once converted. Cairo's density also means a huge amount, from Islamic Cairo's mosques to Coptic Cairo's churches to Khan el-Khalili's bazaar, sits within a relatively compact, walkable-adjacent radius once you're clear of the plateau traffic.
destinations.what_ruined:
The nickel-and-diming is real and it's now unavoidable rather than optional. General plateau admission does not include entry to any pyramid interior, so a family wanting to actually go inside Khufu's chamber is paying 700 EGP plus 1,000 EGP per adult, and virtually every official ticket point has shifted to card-only payment, so travelers who show up assuming Egypt is a cash economy get turned away at the window.

Tout pressure at Giza specifically, the fake gift handoff, the redirect to a 'closed' entrance, the camel ride that balloons in price once you're on the animal and away from the crowd, is persistent enough that most visitors end up either hiring an official guide just to run interference or spending real energy saying no on repeat. Layer on Cairo's traffic, which is a genuine source of stress and delay across the city, and pollution levels that put it among the most polluted major cities measured in 2025, and the qualitative cost of a Cairo trip is higher than the ticket prices alone suggest.
tips: Book Grand Egyptian Museum tickets online in advance only; walk-up purchases stopped when the museum moved to online-only, timed-entry ticketing in December 2025.
Bring a physical credit or debit card for Giza and museum admission; official ticket windows at major sites have gone largely card-only and often will not accept cash pounds.

Budget separately for pyramid interiors: 700 EGP covers general Giza admission, but entering Khufu's Great Pyramid costs an additional 1,000 EGP per foreign adult, Khafre is 280 EGP extra and Menkaure is 200 EGP extra.

Decline any unsolicited 'free' photo, gift or camel-ride offer at the plateau immediately and firmly; the price-switch scam where a cheap-quoted camel or horse ride balloons tenfold once you're mounted is still commonly reported.

Apply for the e-visa only at the official visa2egypt.gov.eg portal; Egypt raised e-visa fees in 2026 to 30 dollars for single entry and 65 dollars for multiple entry, and third-party sites will overcharge on top of that.
Visit between October and March for daytime temperatures around 14 to 22 Celsius; summer months regularly push past 34 to 40 Celsius and coincide with worse smog days in the city center.

guide.title: Cairo Practical Guide: Getting Around, When to Go, and Where to Stay
guide.summary: How to navigate Cairo's metro and traffic, when the weather and crowds actually work in your favor, and where to base yourself for the pyramids, the museum and the old city.
guide.body:
Cairo's metro is the fastest and cheapest way to cross the city, avoiding the traffic that clogs most surface streets for hours a day. As of the March 2026 fare increase, a ride of up to 9 stations costs 10 EGP, up to 16 stations is 12 EGP, up to 23 stations is 15 EGP, and anything longer tops out at 20 EGP, payable with a single paper ticket or a rechargeable contactless card tapped at the gate. For the Giza Plateau itself, which sits outside easy metro reach, ride-hailing apps like Uber and Careem are the more reliable and scam-resistant option over hailing a street taxi, where drivers claiming a 'broken meter' remain one of the most common tourist complaints in the city.

October through March is the peak window for a reason: daytime temperatures sit in a comfortable 14 to 22 Celsius range, though hotel prices and crowds climb accordingly. The shoulder months of March to May and September to November offer a middle ground, with temperatures around 23 to 29 Celsius, thinner crowds, and lower rates. Summer, from roughly May through September, brings dry desert heat that regularly clears 34 Celsius and can exceed 40 Celsius at midday, which combines poorly with the plateau's shadeless open terrain and the city's traffic-driven smog.

Zamalek, the leafy island neighborhood on the Nile, is the most common base for visitors who want quieter streets and easy river access, while Downtown Cairo and Garden City sit closer to the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir and Khan El-Khalili bazaar in Islamic Cairo. Staying near Giza itself cuts commute time to the pyramids and the new museum but puts you farther from the old city's mosques, churches and market streets. For money-saving moves, carry a card for all official admissions since cash is increasingly refused at ticket windows, keep smaller Egyptian-pound cash on hand specifically for baksheesh, roughly 20 to 50 EGP for informal help at smaller mosques or Coptic churches, and confirm any e-visa purchase is going through the official government portal rather than a marked-up third-party reseller.

rating_rationale.overall: The Grand Egyptian Museum plus the pyramids is a legitimately world-class pairing, but constant tout pressure and card-only ticketing friction keep it from a perfect score.
rating_rationale.safety: US State Department rates Egypt Level 2 with Cairo outside the Do Not Travel zones, but periodic embassy security alerts and dense petty-crime/scam pressure at tourist sites warrant real caution.
rating_rationale.value: Admission prices are still modest by global capital standards, but 2026 fee hikes across e-visas, metro fares and site tickets, plus separate interior-access charges, add up faster than the headline numbers suggest.

facts_checked: Grand Egyptian Museum opened to the public on November 4, 2025, and moved to online-only, timed-entry ticketing (no walk-up purchases) by December 2025.
Grand Egyptian Museum foreign adult admission is approximately 1,500 EGP (about 30 USD at 2026 rates); Egyptian nationals pay 200 EGP.
Giza Plateau general admission is 700 EGP for foreign adults and 350 EGP for foreign students; children under 6 are free.
Entering the Great Pyramid of Khufu costs an additional 1,000 EGP for foreign adults (500 EGP for students), on top of the 700 EGP plateau entry.
Khafre pyramid interior access is an additional 280 EGP; Menkaure pyramid interior access is an additional 200 EGP.
Most official Egyptian tourist-site ticket windows have shifted to card/online payment, with cash increasingly not accepted at major site ticket booths.

Common Giza-area tourist scams include the unsolicited 'free photo/gift then demand payment' trick, the fake 'closed entrance' redirect, and camel/horse rides quoted cheap then repriced far higher after the ride.
Cairo ranked among the world's most polluted major cities in September and October 2025, per IQAir; 2024 annual PM2.5 averaged 39.9 micrograms per cubic meter (AQI ~111), about 8x the WHO guideline.
Road transport accounts for roughly 33% of Cairo's PM2.5 pollution, with an aging vehicle fleet contributing heavily to traffic congestion.

US State Department rates Egypt Level 2, 'Exercise Increased Caution,' with Do Not Travel guidance limited to Northern/Middle Sinai and parts of the Western Desert; Cairo tourist sites fall outside those zones.
US Embassy Cairo issued periodic security alerts through early-to-mid 2026 advising heightened public-space caution.
Egypt raised tourist e-visa fees in 2026 to 30 USD for single entry (up from 25 USD) and 65 USD for multiple entry (up from 60 USD); single-entry visas are valid 3 months for a 30-day stay.
Cairo Metro fares increased March 27, 2026: 10 EGP (up to 9 stations), 12 EGP (10-16 stations), 15 EGP (17-23 stations), 20 EGP (24+ stations).
USD/EGP exchange rate traded roughly in the low-to-mid 50s (around 51-54 EGP per dollar) through early-to-mid 2026.
Egypt's annual inflation rate was about 14.3% in June 2026, down slightly from 14.6% in May 2026.
Best weather window for Cairo is October through March, with daytime temperatures around 14-22C (57-72F); summer (May-September) daytime highs commonly exceed 34C and can pass 40C (104F).

destinations.name: Cancun
destinations.summary: Cancun in 2026 is fighting its worst sargassum year on record and pricier all-inclusive resorts, with real upside limited to the clearer beaches on Isla Mujeres, Costa Mujeres and Holbox.
destinations.headline: Cancun 2026: Record Sargassum, Pricier Resorts and a New Tourist Tax You Have to Pay Yourself
destinations.body:
Cancun in 2026 is having one of its worst sargassum years on record, and that single fact should shape how you plan the trip. Early arrivals of the brown seaweed were confirmed as far back as January and March 2026, and by late June, 92.5 percent of monitored beaches in Quintana Roo were registering excessive sargassum accumulation. The mess is not evenly spread. Playa del Carmen, Tulum, Sian Ka'an and the stretch between Cancun and Puerto Morelos have taken the worst of it, while Holbox, Isla Mujeres, Costa Mujeres and the west coast of Cozumel have stayed comparatively clear through mid-2026. Mexico's federal government is spending $115 million through 2026 on collection vessels, offshore barriers and monitoring to intercept the algae before it rots on the sand, and hotel operators are separately spending an estimated $150 million a year on private raking crews, barriers and hauling equipment. It has not been enough to stop hotels from cutting room rates by as much as 40 percent in the hardest-hit stretches, and one estimate puts the potential GDP hit to affected coastal areas at 11 percent.

None of this makes Cancun cheap. Budget all-inclusive resorts are running $150 to $270 per person per night, mid-range properties $300 to $550 per person per night, and luxury resorts $650 to $1,250 or more per person per night, with overall resort pricing up roughly 25 percent since 2024. A couple can still find a basic Hotel Zone all-inclusive room for $200 to $400 a night, but anything resembling the marketing photos on a chain resort's website runs $400 to $900-plus a night for two. On top of the room rate, every non-Mexican visitor to Quintana Roo now owes the Visitax, 285 pesos, or roughly $15, which as of 2026 is not collected by hotels and must be paid online in advance, with a QR code as the only accepted proof at departure.

The other tax on your vacation is time. Timeshare touts working the airport arrivals hall and the Hotel Zone sidewalks still pitch a free breakfast, day pass or excursion in exchange for what they call a 90-minute presentation, but multiple recent traveler reports describe the pitch running four to six hours and ending in contracts as large as $25,000, hundreds of which Mexico's consumer protection agency PROFECO has since annulled. Quintana Roo authorities have also identified up to 20 new fake hotel booking websites appearing every month, and in February 2025 the U.S. Treasury sanctioned a timeshare resale fraud network tied to the CJNG cartel that has been linked to more than $288 million in losses among timeshare owners contacted by fake resale brokers.

Weather and safety add two more variables. Hurricane season runs the official June 1 to November 30 window, with the real risk window mid-August through late October and the statistical peak around September 10; 2026 forecasters are calling for a near-normal to below-normal season as a developing El Nino increases wind shear over the Caribbean. On safety, the U.S. State Department kept Quintana Roo at its Level 2, exercise increased caution, advisory as of late May 2026, citing organized-crime violence in which bystanders have occasionally been caught in crossfire between rival groups, alongside the more mundane risk of pickpocketing and petty theft that any resort-heavy tourist zone attracts.
destinations.what_great:
Cancun's appeal is still real even in a rough sargassum year. Isla Mujeres, Costa Mujeres and Holbox were reporting comparatively clear water through mid-2026, and they are all a short ferry or drive from the Hotel Zone, so a bad beach day at your resort does not have to be the whole trip. Nonstop flights from dozens of U.S. and Canadian cities keep travel time short, the Hotel Zone's infrastructure of buses, taxis, pharmacies and restaurants at every price point is dense and easy to navigate without a rental car, and the all-inclusive model, whatever its price creep, still removes the guesswork of budgeting every meal and drink on a foreign trip.

The region's Mayan ruins, cenotes and reef diving around Cozumel and Puerto Morelos remain legitimately excellent and are largely unaffected by the sargassum problem, since it is a beach and nearshore issue rather than one that touches inland attractions or most open-water reef sites.
destinations.what_ruined:
The sargassum situation in 2026 is the headline problem: with over 90 percent of monitored Quintana Roo beaches showing excessive accumulation by late June, plenty of travelers are paying resort prices for a beach they cannot actually swim from without wading through brown mats of rotting algae, and the smell as it decomposes is a real complaint, not an exaggeration. Budget travelers are also getting squeezed from multiple directions at once: all-inclusive rates are up about 25 percent since 2024, the mandatory 285-peso Visitax now has to be paid separately online rather than folded into the hotel bill, and airport arrivals still have to run a gauntlet of timeshare touts whose free offers reliably turn into four to six hour pressure pitches.

Layer on a Level 2 U.S. State Department advisory for organized-crime-related violence in Quintana Roo, a hurricane season that runs June through November with its real risk concentrated August through October, and a wave of fake hotel booking websites, with authorities finding around 20 new ones a month, that can leave travelers with a canceled reservation at check-in, and Cancun in 2026 requires considerably more homework than the postcard version suggests.
tips: Book a hotel in Isla Mujeres, Costa Mujeres or Holbox instead of the southern Hotel Zone if beach time matters, since those areas were reporting the clearest water on the Quintana Roo coast through mid-2026 while Playa del Carmen and Tulum saw the worst sargassum.
Pay the 285-peso (about $15) Visitax online before you fly since hotels stopped collecting it in 2026; you need the QR code it generates as proof of payment, and cash is not accepted.

Decline any free breakfast or free excursion offer tied to a timeshare tour at the airport or in the Hotel Zone; the advertised 90-minute presentation regularly runs four to six hours and has produced contracts as large as $25,000, hundreds of which Mexico's consumer agency PROFECO has annulled.

Verify your hotel reservation directly with the property before you fly; Quintana Roo authorities have been finding roughly 20 new fake hotel booking websites a month, and some travelers have arrived at check-in to find no record of their booking.

If traveling between mid-August and late October, buy travel insurance with hurricane and weather coverage, since that window covers the statistical peak of Atlantic hurricane season around September 10.

Do not assume a low headline rate covers everything; budget all-inclusive resorts running $150 to $270 per person per night in 2026 is the low end, and overall pricing across every tier is running about 25 percent above 2024 levels.

guide.title: Cancun Travel Guide 2026: Where to Stay, When to Go and How to Avoid the Traps
guide.summary: A practical planning guide to Cancun's Hotel Zone, downtown and ferry towns, built around the specific 2026 factors, sargassum, the Visitax and timeshare touts, that actually change your itinerary.
guide.body:
Getting around Cancun does not require a rental car unless you plan to explore ruins or cenotes well outside the city. The R1 and R2 public buses run the length of Avenida Kukulkan through the Hotel Zone for a few pesos and are the cheapest way to move between resorts, downtown Cancun and the ferry terminals. Taxis inside the Hotel Zone are unmetered and routinely overcharge tourists, so agree on a price before getting in or use an app-based ride option where available. Ferries to Isla Mujeres run regularly from Puerto Juarez and from the Hotel Zone's Playa Tortugas and Playa Caracol docks, and that island is worth the trip given how much clearer its water has stayed compared with the mainland beaches in 2026.

On timing, the driest and least humid months are typically December through April, which is also the highest-demand and highest-price stretch. Late spring and early summer bring lower prices but rising sargassum risk building toward what forecasters expect to be a record or near-record year. Hurricane season runs June through November, with the real risk concentrated mid-August to late October, so anyone booking that window should factor in cancellation insurance.

For neighborhoods, the Hotel Zone is the resort strip most visitors picture, walkable in sections but spread over roughly 14 miles of a narrow barrier island, while downtown Cancun, known locally as El Centro, is where residents actually live, with far cheaper food and none of the beach access. Money-saving moves that actually work: book a resort on Isla Mujeres, Costa Mujeres or the northern Hotel Zone near Punta Cancun where sargassum has historically been lighter, pay the Visitax online in advance rather than dealing with it at the airport, and treat every unsolicited free tour offer as a timeshare pitch, because that is almost always exactly what it is.

rating_rationale.overall: Still a legitimate beach destination with real upside on the outer islands, but 2026's record-level sargassum and rising costs mean it no longer matches its all-inclusive marketing image.
rating_rationale.safety: Level 2 U.S. State Department advisory for organized-crime activity as of May 2026, plus routine but non-violent theft and timeshare pressure; tourists are not typically the direct targets of the worst violence.
rating_rationale.value: All-inclusive pricing is up about 25 percent since 2024, a mandatory $15 Visitax is now a separate line item paid online, and much of what you're paying for, a clean beach, is compromised in 2026 by the worst sargassum season on record.

destinations.name: Cape Town
destinations.summary: Cape Town combines Table Mountain, Cape Peninsula beaches and the Winelands with a food scene now anchored by Time Out Market and the V&A Waterfront, but a clear-eyed visitor needs real facts on crime hotspots, airport taxi scams and the city's power and water history before booking.
destinations.headline: Cape Town 2026 Travel Guide: Table Mountain, Wine Country and Beaches, Plus the Safety and Power Facts Visitors Actually Need
destinations.body:
Cape Town's signature draw remains Table Mountain, reached by the Aerial Cableway for R475 per adult and R230 per child on a return ticket booked online, roughly 10 percent cheaper than buying at the ticket office. From the summit plateau, visitors get panoramic views over the city bowl, Table Bay and the Atlantic seaboard suburbs of Camps Bay, Clifton and Sea Point, all considered safe to walk in daylight. A short drive out of the city opens onto the Cape Winelands, where a full day guided tour through Stellenbosch and Franschhoek runs about R1,400 to R2,500 per person, roughly 80 to 145 US dollars, including transport, tastings and lunch, typically departing Cape Town around 9am and returning by early evening.

The food scene has matured well beyond wine country. The V&A Waterfront now hosts more than 80 restaurants, bars and cafes, including the newer Time Out Market Cape Town, which features Cape Malay focused Barakat, the shisanyama inspired MLILO and a ramen outpost from World's 50 Best nominated FYN. Across town, the Old Biscuit Mill's Neighbourgoods Market, running since 2006, has grown into a Saturday institution with dozens of food vendors and live music.

Safety requires more nuance than blanket warnings suggest. Township areas such as Nyanga and Khayelitsha, along with parts of the Cape Flats, see genuinely high crime rates and are not suited to independent tourist visits outside a reputable guided tour, while gang violence there mostly stays within local communities rather than spilling into tourist zones. The roads immediately around Cape Town International Airport are a specific hotspot, and the US Embassy issued a warning in February 2026 about fake taxi operators targeting new arrivals there, recommending app booked rides picked up only from the designated rank. Within the city, locals generally avoid walking alone at night anywhere except the V&A Waterfront promenade, defaulting to Uber instead.

On infrastructure, Eskom's April 2026 winter outlook, covering April through August, removed the Western Cape from load shedding schedules entirely, following a run of 341 consecutive days without outages nationally, a marked change from the rolling blackouts of prior years. Cape Town's other defining crisis, the 2015 to 2018 drought that nearly triggered Day Zero water shutoffs when the Theewaterskloof Dam fell to roughly 10 percent capacity, is now history: the dam recovered to 100 percent by October 2020 and normal water use has continued since, though the episode still shapes local attitudes toward conservation.
destinations.what_great: Cape Town delivers a genuinely rare combination for one city: a cable car ride to a flat-topped mountain summit with sweeping ocean views, Blue Flag beaches at Camps Bay and Clifton within a 15 minute drive of downtown, and a Winelands day trip through Stellenbosch and Franschhoek that ranks among the most scenic wine regions anywhere. The dining scene has caught up too, with Time Out Market Cape Town and the long running Neighbourgoods Market giving visitors an easy, low stakes way to sample Cape Malay, African and international cooking side by side, and the current absence of scheduled load shedding means none of it is likely to be interrupted by a power cut.
destinations.what_ruined: The honest friction is that safety in Cape Town is genuinely uneven rather than overhyped or underhyped. Tourist zones like the V&A Waterfront, Camps Bay and Sea Point are low risk in daylight, but the roads around the airport are an active hotspot for fake taxi scams serious enough that the US Embassy warned about them in February 2026, and township areas like Khayelitsha and Nyanga carry real crime risk that makes independent visits unwise. Layer on the fact that almost nobody, local or visitor, walks alone at night outside the Waterfront, and a trip that looks purely scenic in photos requires constant low level logistics planning around transport that a first timer may not expect.
tips: Table Mountain Aerial Cableway online return tickets cost R475 for adults and R230 for children, about 10 percent cheaper than buying at the ticket office on the day.
Eskom's April 2026 winter outlook, covering April through August, took the Western Cape off load shedding schedules entirely after 341 consecutive days without outages nationally.

The US Embassy warned in February 2026 about fake taxi operators targeting arrivals at Cape Town International Airport, so book rides only through an app and collect them from the designated pickup point.

US, UK, EU, Canadian and Australian passport holders can enter South Africa visa free for up to 90 days, provided the passport is valid at least 30 days beyond the exit date and has two consecutive blank visa pages.

A guided full day wine tour to Stellenbosch and Franschhoek typically costs R1,400 to R2,500 per person, roughly 80 to 145 US dollars including transport, tastings and lunch, departing Cape Town around 9am and returning by early evening.

guide.title: Cape Town Practical Guide: Getting There, When to Go and What to Budget
guide.summary: A practical rundown of when to visit, where to base a stay, what to budget and which parts of the city are worth skipping.
guide.body:
Most international visitors fly into Cape Town International Airport, where the airport road corridor is a known crime hotspot and app booked transport from the official rank is the safer default over hailing a cab curbside. Cape Town's seasons run opposite to the Northern Hemisphere: the dry summer from November through March brings the most consistent sunshine and the busiest, most expensive crowds, especially in January, while winter from June through August is cooler and wetter, with 60 to 100mm of rain a month from Atlantic cold fronts. Autumn, March through May, is widely considered the best value window, with warm settled weather around 18 to 26 degrees Celsius, calmer winds and lighter crowds than peak summer.

For a first stay, Sea Point, Green Point and the V&A Waterfront offer walkable, well lit bases close to restaurants and within daylight walking distance of the Waterfront's shops and markets, while Camps Bay and Clifton suit travelers prioritizing beach access over city center convenience. Budget for the Table Mountain cableway at R475 per adult return, a Winelands day tour at R1,400 to R2,500 per person, and app based rides for essentially all after dark movement, since walking alone at night is not standard practice even for residents outside the Waterfront promenade. Must do experiences include the cableway or a Platteklip Gorge hike up Table Mountain, a Stellenbosch and Franschhoek wine day, and a stop at Neighbourgoods Market or Time Out Market Cape Town for a single meal sampling multiple kitchens. What to avoid: independent, unguided visits to Cape Flats townships like Khayelitsha or Nyanga, curbside taxi touts at the airport rather than app booked or official rank rides, and assuming current load shedding relief is permanent, since South Africa's grid has reversed course before.

rating_rationale.overall: Table Mountain, the Winelands and a genuinely strong food scene combine into one of the most complete city trips in Africa, held back only by the extra planning safety requires.
rating_rationale.safety: Core tourist areas are safe in daylight and load shedding risk is currently low, but airport taxi scams and no-go township areas mean visitors cannot treat the city like a low vigilance destination.
rating_rationale.value: A R475 cableway ticket and a full day Winelands tour for under 150 US dollars make premium experiences accessible, though app based transport costs add up for visitors avoiding walking at night.

destinations.name: Cartagena
destinations.summary: The walled city is genuinely beautiful, but everything inside it runs 40 to 50 percent above Getsemani prices, and the heat, cruise-day crowds and petty theft are all real, not exaggerated.
destinations.headline: Cartagena's Walled City Is Stunning and a Tourist Markup Machine at the Same Time
destinations.body: Cartagena's Ciudad Amurallada, the UNESCO-listed walled city, is one of the best-preserved colonial cores in the Americas, and the postcard version of it is accurate: pastel facades, bougainvillea over wrought-iron balconies, and eleven kilometers of 16th and 17th century Spanish fortifications ringing the old town. What guidebooks undersell is the price gap between that walled core and Getsemani, the formerly rough neighborhood next door that gentrified into the city's actual value zone. Multiple current cost breakdowns put walled-city dining and lodging 40 to 50 percent above Getsemani for comparable quality. On the street level that plays out in specifics: empanadas run about 1,000 to 2,000 pesos, arepas with cheese or meat around 3,000 to 5,000 pesos, and a full lunch plate at a local fonda 8,000 to 12,000 pesos, while a casual sit-down meal in Getsemani runs 15,000 to 25,000 pesos and climbs sharply once you cross into the walled city's restaurant rows. Budget travelers based in Getsemani hostels report daily costs around 60 to 85 euros; walled-city boutique hotel stays with restaurant dining run 120 to 160 euros a day, and colonial-mansion luxury properties inside the walls run 250 to 400 euros. Hotel listings inside the walled city itself start around 44 to 63 dollars a night for basic 3 and 4 star rooms and climb past 122 dollars for historic boutique properties. The climate is not a minor inconvenience: average humidity sits around 82 percent year round, dipping to 79 percent in February and peaking near 83 percent in October, and while February and March are technically the hottest months with highs near 32 degrees Celsius, April, May and September combine similar heat with peak humidity and feel worse on the ground. The rainy season runs May through November against a drier window from December through April. Safety is a real conversation, not scare-mongering: the U.S. State Department has kept Colombia at a Level 3, Reconsider Travel advisory citing crime, terrorism, civil unrest and kidnapping risk nationally, even though the U.S. Embassy in Bogota separately describes Cartagena as the country's safest major tourist destination. Inside the tourist zones the real risks are pickpocketing, phone snatching, ATM skimming, and taxi overcharging, along with warnings about scopolamine drink-spiking and fake-police scams that show up repeatedly in embassy and traveler advisories. Cruise crowding is also intensifying rather than easing: Cartagena's 2025 to 2026 cruise season was projected to bring in roughly 365,214 passengers across 182 port calls through late June 2026, a jump of about 26 percent, with Royal Caribbean alone committing 36 port calls and around 82,800 combined embarking and disembarking passengers, so a port day inside the walls can mean thousands of extra day-trippers moving through the same few blocks. One recent, tangible change: on December 29, 2025, the city banned the horse-drawn carriages that had circled the walled city for decades, replacing them with a fleet of 62 imported electric carriages, with the same drivers largely retained.
destinations.what_great:
The walled city and its fortifications are the real deal, an intact colonial defensive complex that took over two centuries to build, and walking it at dusk when the heat breaks is worth the trip on its own. Getsemani has genuinely absorbed the street art, live music and casual food scene that used to define the old town before it gentrified, and it delivers most of the same atmosphere for meaningfully less money, per current cost comparisons. The city is compact and walkable, the historic core is mostly flat and increasingly pedestrian-priority, and Cartagena's tourist zones carry a real reputation, backed by the U.S. Embassy, as the safest major tourist draw in Colombia.

Getting around beyond walking is workable and often cheap: Uber functions in the city even though it sits in a legal gray area in Colombia, InDriver lets you counter-propose a fare and frequently comes in 20 to 30 percent below Uber, and both tend to beat unmetered taxis on price and predictability if you agree on a fare or use the app rate up front.
destinations.what_ruined:
The walled city runs a straightforward tourist tax: the same meal, room or tour costs 40 to 50 percent more inside the walls than a five minute walk away in Getsemani, and a lot of visitors never realize they're paying it. Heat and humidity are not seasonal color, they are a near constant, averaging 82 percent humidity year round with only a narrow window, December through April, that counts as comparatively dry. Petty crime targeting tourists, phone snatching, pickpocketing, ATM skimming, distraction theft and inflated taxi fares, is common enough that it shows up across nearly every current safety guide and the U.S. Embassy's own advisories, alongside specific scopolamine drink-spiking warnings.

Cruise-day crowding is getting worse, not better, with the 2025 to 2026 season projected up roughly 26 percent in passenger volume, so timing a visit around the port schedule genuinely changes how the walled city feels. Colombia also carries a blanket Level 3, Reconsider Travel advisory from the U.S. State Department for the country as a whole, which is a real data point even though it is driven mostly by regions far from Cartagena's tourist core, and taxis still don't run meters, so every ride is a negotiation unless you use an app.
tips: Base yourself in Getsemani, not the walled city: current cost breakdowns show a 40 to 50 percent price gap between the two for comparable hotels and restaurants.
Budget street food realistically: empanadas run about 1,000 to 2,000 pesos and a full fonda lunch plate 8,000 to 12,000 pesos, versus 15,000 to 25,000 pesos for a casual sit-down meal.
Avoid February through May and September if you're heat sensitive; average humidity runs 79 to 83 percent year round and those months combine peak heat with peak humidity.
Use Uber or InDriver instead of street taxis; taxis don't run meters and require negotiating a fare before you get in, while InDriver fares typically run 20 to 30 percent below Uber.
Check the cruise port schedule before booking your walled-city time; the 2025 to 2026 season is running roughly 26 percent higher in passenger volume than the prior season.
Keep your phone in a zipped pocket, not your hand, in the walled city and Getsemani; phone snatching and pickpocketing are the most commonly reported tourist crimes, per embassy and safety reports.

guide.title: Cartagena Practical Guide: Neighborhoods, Timing and Getting Around
guide.summary: Where to base yourself, when to go, and how to move around Cartagena without overpaying or overheating.
guide.body:
Cartagena splits into a few distinct zones that matter more for planning than the guidebooks suggest. The walled Ciudad Amurallada is the postcard core, dense with restored colonial mansions, boutique hotels and restaurants, and it charges accordingly, with current pricing showing a 40 to 50 percent premium over neighboring Getsemani for comparable quality. Getsemani, just outside the walls, has its own dense grid of street art, live music bars and casual restaurants and has become the better-value base for most travelers without losing much walkable proximity to the old town. Bocagrande, the high-rise beach strip south of the old city, is a separate, more modern zone popular with domestic tourists and less connected to the colonial-city experience most visitors come for.

Timing matters more in Cartagena than in a lot of Caribbean destinations because the climate barely varies month to month in temperature but swings hard in rainfall and crowding. The dry season runs roughly December through April and is the most comfortable window for walking the walls and the old town, while the wet season runs May through November. Humidity sits around 82 percent essentially year round, so even the 'cooler' months feel muggy; February and March post the highest recorded highs, but April, May and September combine strong heat with peak humidity and are frequently described as feeling worse on the ground. Cruise ship schedules are worth checking independently of weather: the 2025 to 2026 season brought a projected 26 percent jump in passenger volume, and a heavy port day can visibly change how crowded the walled city's main plazas and shopping streets feel by mid-morning.

Getting around is straightforward. The walled city and Getsemani are compact, mostly flat and easy to cover on foot, and as of December 29, 2025, the old horse-drawn carriages that circled the walls were replaced with a fleet of 62 electric carriages, with most of the original drivers retained. For anything farther, Uber operates in the city despite functioning in a legal gray area in Colombia, and often beats street taxi pricing; InDriver, where you propose your own fare and drivers accept or counter, frequently comes in 20 to 30 percent cheaper than Uber. Traditional taxis remain common but don't use meters, so agree on a price before the ride starts rather than after. For money, expect an exchange rate in the neighborhood of 3,100 to 3,200 pesos to the U.S. dollar, and know that Migracion Colombia updated its administrative fee schedule under Resolution 0599, effective February 10, 2026, which raised several visa and tourist-stamp related fees, so travelers extending a stay should check current rates rather than relying on older figures.

rating_rationale.overall: An intact, walkable colonial city with real fortifications and a genuinely better-value neighborhood next door, offset by heavy tourist pricing and cruise crowding.
rating_rationale.safety: Tourist zones are comparatively safe per the U.S. Embassy, but Colombia sits at a national Level 3 advisory and phone theft, pickpocketing and scam reports are common in the walled city and Getsemani.
rating_rationale.value: Walled-city prices run 40 to 50 percent above Getsemani for comparable quality, so value swings hard based on which few blocks you choose to stay and eat in.
